## TL;DR

I completed the Releases cut-flow pass at desktop width (1280 × 900) and phone width (375 × 812). The notes chooser, blocker, running, failed, and successful states remained understandable and usable. At 375px, long content scrolls inside the cut drawer while the Publish/Cancel footer remains visible. No product bug surfaced, so I made no UI change and did not need to add a product regression test. I added a repeatable headless Playwright harness and the requested QA record. The run intercepted release APIs and recorded zero release POSTs.

## Work and rationale

I first read the Releases view, the existing release cut-flow tests, the release preview fixtures, the UI preview conventions, and the prior release/restart QA report. Existing component tests already cover the Cut Next shortcut, notes generation choices, saved drafts, and form persistence. This pass therefore focused on the user-visible rendered flow and the requested boundary conditions at two widths, rather than duplicating component-level behavior.

I created `docs/qa/measure-releases-cut-flow.mjs` as a small reproducible browser pass. The script starts headless Chromium and intercepts `/api/release*` calls with synthetic state. It supplies a ready status, dirty-tree blocker, running check, failed check with test output, and successful run. It opens the notes chooser without confirming note generation. The release POST handler increments a safety counter and the script fails if that counter is nonzero. Thus the exercise can inspect the UI without contacting the real release path.

The browser matrix covers 1280 × 900 and 375 × 812 for each of the five states. It asserts there is no horizontal overflow, the chooser's options and primary action fit in the viewport, the blocked state disables the cut entry, the running state names the current step, the failed state surfaces its summary, and the successful state shows the outcome. It also records uncaught page errors and verifies that the drawer footer does not fall below the viewport.

The requested retained record is `docs/qa/2026-11-releases-cut-flow.md`. It documents the execution method, test matrix, evidence boundaries, and the zero-mutation result. Screenshots were captured under the ignored `.repoos/qa-releases-cut-flow/` directory. I visually inspected the 375px chooser, failed, and successful captures and kept all screenshot binaries out of the branch.

## Approaches tried

I first tried waiting for `networkidle` before interacting with the page. That stalled because the app maintains its event stream, so network idle is not a useful readiness condition here. I changed the harness to wait for `domcontentloaded`, then wait for the actual drawer and controls. This made the run deterministic without changing application code.

The first script run also used Playwright's default `data-testid` lookup, while RepoOS uses `data-test-id`. I switched those checks to explicit CSS selectors matching the project convention. These were harness issues, not application defects.

I initially inspected the failure state at a 900px height. The screenshot made the footer seem close to the lower edge, so I added direct geometry checks and then reran with a more phone-like 812px height. Measurements confirmed the footer stays at the viewport bottom, while `.drawer-body` owns the overflow. The failed state remains scrollable without displacing Publish and Cancel.

## Challenges and blockers

The server keeps an event stream open, which prevents a `networkidle` navigation condition from settling. Waiting for the app shell and controls instead resolved that problem.

The dirty-tree fixture deliberately allows opening the drawer through its deep link even though the page-level cut button is disabled. That is useful for checking the explanatory disabled-state copy and the drawer's own `canOpen` guard, but it means the browser scenario tests fixture rendering rather than attempting to bypass a real server gate. No release operation was confirmed or invoked.

I used a detached scratch worktree under this task worktree for the auth-less server, matching the QA isolation requirement. Its build completed, and the browser checks ran against loopback only. The scratch worktree and generated screenshots are ignored local artifacts; only the QA script and prose report are intended for the task branch.

## Key learnings

For this app, a browser harness should not use `networkidle` as its page-ready signal because the event stream can stay open indefinitely. Waiting for a route-specific UI element is more reliable and gives a better error if the screen does not mount.

The release drawer already has the mobile behavior this pass was meant to verify: its body scrolls independently and its action strip remains anchored to the bottom. This held even in the failed state, with the summary, tl;dr, failed-test link, command output, and Debugger action all present.

The current preview fixtures and component tests provide strong state coverage, but this rendered pass adds evidence for actual viewport geometry and for the no-mutation boundary. Keeping the intercept and assertions in a committed script makes it possible to rerun the same QA without exposing a real publish endpoint.

The final `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed. It classified this branch as a docs/bookkeeping-only diff, so unrelated build, lint, test, and UI smoke steps were skipped. Formatting, branch-artifact, task-asset, and task-parser checks passed. I did not stage or commit files; RepoOS owns task-branch finalization.
